protocol: Author annotation. 30 trajectories sampled (seed 3), one handoff position each (seed 7, uniform over steps 2..N-2); every extracted future-relevant anchor (capped at 8 per trajectory by deterministic stride subsampling) inspected with prefix and suffix context windows; judged TP if the string denotes a genuine task-level entity/quantity/artifact/answer AND the suffix occurrence re-references the same referent; FP if scaffold/chrome vocabulary, extraction artifact, or accidental collision.

iterations.action: largest FP families: generic unigram entities (entity precision 0.42), framework/chrome vocabulary, number fragments (UUID/phone/time). Added common-English-word filter, scaffold stoplist, scaffold-context suppression, number hyphen/leading-zero rules, entity sub-span dedup.
fixed trim-to-single-word leak, code-keyword entities, metadata window 30->60, quote possessive-split and template-escape artifacts, more common words.
fixed article-retention bug, further vocabulary; declared tuning converged.

fresh sample surfaced mechanical families: JSON/dict key tokens, f-string URL templates, strftime formats, dotted code identifiers, harness files (scenario.py), epoch/app-id metadata, doubled-word spans. Applied mechanical fixes + clearly generic vocabulary. NOTE: after this step the second sample is no longer a pure holdout.

iterations.residual_fp_families: page-sidebar/chrome entities on re-scraped web pages (~17), generic vocabulary (~10), cross-referent string collisions (~6), code parameter values (~5), clipped spans (~6).

high_precision_subset.use: reported as a sensitivity variant: fidelity recomputed on url/file/number/answer anchors only

final.collision_note: the ground-truth-answer anchor rule can collide (a date '11' matching a count '11'); with n=2 answer anchors in the audited sample its precision estimate (0.5) is uninformative but the failure mode is disclosed.
